ReportFlow Pro v8.2 • Current Build
Built From Real Reporting Problems

ReportFlow Pro

Multi-industry reporting, focused QA/QC & operational visibility

ReportFlow is built for companies living in Excel but tired of sending raw workbooks around as the finished product. It keeps the workbook as the source, identifies what kind of job it is looking at, and turns the relevant data into something people can actually review and deliver.

The big change: ReportFlow no longer treats every sheet and field like it belongs to every job. The Profile Engine identifies the industry and job/test configuration first. Mapped requirements can create findings; uncertain layouts are marked Review instead of being reported as false failures.
Talk About Company Setup →Open ReportFlow
What It Can Do Now

One reporting engine, different workflows.

The environmental/stack-testing profile is the first fully tuned production pack. General business operations are active, with additional industry frameworks ready to be trained around real company forms and requirements.

Smart IntakeImport operational Excel and CSV files

Reads existing company workbooks, supports flexible column mapping, saves reusable datasets, and keeps the original source workbook unchanged.

Profile EngineDetect the industry and job/test type first

Routes the workbook into the right profile before applying specialized checks. Unknown or unfamiliar layouts are held for review instead of being forced into the wrong rules.

QA/QCRun only relevant checks

Applies focused rule packs to the active configuration, separates passed checks from warnings and critical items, and avoids flagging inactive template material as missing data.

Stack TestingCreate preliminary client-facing reports

Pulls actual runs, emissions results, standards, pollutant worksheets, RM-vs-CEMS comparisons, relative accuracy, bias and PASS / FAIL / REVIEW status into a clean preliminary package.

Part 60 RATAFocused Part 60 worksheet selection

Recognizes Part 60 RATA summary sheets and excludes hidden Part 75, helper, calculation, ERT and unused parameter tabs from the preliminary report and irrelevant missing-input checks.

Business ReportingDashboards, KPIs, trends and exceptions

Tracks projects, status, dates, labor, revenue/value, operational filters, threshold exceptions, performance trends and management reporting outside the stack-testing workflow.

Report ControlSave, brand, print and reuse reports

Includes saved report registers, reusable templates, company branding, report titles and print-ready output so teams can deliver a report instead of the working spreadsheet.

ManagementRoles, users and activity history

Provides Owner, Admin, Manager, Analyst and Viewer role structure, company user management, activity logging, custom KPIs and configurable exception rules.

Recurring WorkScheduled reporting workflow

Stores recurring report schedules and calculates upcoming run dates. Cloud-based automatic generation and email delivery are the next backend phase rather than an over-promised current feature.

How It Works

A straightforward process.

You do not need to show up with technical specs. Start with the problem, and we work from there.

1. Tell me the problem.

What is slowing your team down? What are you tracking manually? What gets missed, repeated or scattered?

2. Define the workflow.

We map out how the work is actually being done today and what a better process should look like.

3. Build the right tool.

Instead of forcing your company into generic software, I build a solution around the way your operation works.

4. Test and improve it.

The best tools get better with real use. We refine what matters and keep improving the system.

About

The background behind the build.

Gulf Coast Code Works is rooted in real operations experience, not just theory.

Travis Hebert

Owner & Developer

Hi, I’m Travis

Real operations experience, applied to software.

My professional background is rooted in project management, environmental testing and industrial field operations. I’ve spent years coordinating people, equipment, schedules, technical requirements, clients, data quality and deadlines.

That experience is what pushed me toward software development. Too many businesses still rely on disconnected spreadsheets, paper forms, group texts and repetitive manual entry for work that deserves a better system. I build software around the way the operation actually runs instead of forcing the operation to fit somebody else’s software.

I’m continuing to expand my software and web-development work through practical applications, workflow systems, mobile tools, dashboards and business-process automation. My approach is personal and straightforward: understand the problem first, build what’s useful, test it in the real world, and keep improving it.

Project & Operations LeadershipTeams, equipment, scheduling, clients and execution.
Environmental & Industrial ExperienceField work, regulated workflows, QA/QC and reporting.
Software & Web DevelopmentApplications, interfaces, logic, testing and deployment.
